title: Same name, different maths
hook: Two nodes called NAG differ by one on the same slider. Blue noise isn't always blue. Our reading of packs' source found names you can't trust, so read the formula.

verified.claim: Core's NAG uses z_pos × scale − z_neg × (scale − 1).
sd-perturbed-attention's NAG uses z_pos + scale × (z_pos − z_neg).
With σ = 1, flux_time_shift at μ equals time_snr_shift at α = e^μ.
Core's perp is neg minus its projection on pos, and bvhari's variable named perp is pos projected on neg.
verified.ref: comfy_extras/nodes_perpneg.py, bvhari/ComfyUI_PerpNeg perpneg.py, read as text

verified.claim: PowerNoiseSuite's blue_noise defaults to alpha 2 and divides the FFT by the square root of (fx² + fy²)^(alpha/2).
BasicScheduler keeps the step count at low denoise, and AlignYourSteps cuts it to round(steps × denoise).
The sampler named ddim runs euler with an inpaint option, and our one-seed renders matched pixel for pixel.
Both graphs pass validate_prompt, and nm_sigmas ran on a CPU.
Core's NAG sets an attn1 output patch and reads z_pos and z_neg from the CFG batch. sd-perturbed-attention replaces attn2 and runs its own negative attention.
verified.ref: comfy_extras/nodes_nag.py, pamparamm/sd-perturbed-attention nag_nodes.py, read as text
